newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber easier at close in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber easier at close in slow trade.

text.p: Rubber futures were easier at the close on Tuesday despite moderate shortcovering by rubber manufacturers from Thailand, dealers said.
"We believe some manufacturers from Thailand were engaged in moderate shortcovering for their monthly rubber requirements," a local rubber trader said.
The manufacturers bought about nearly 1,300 tonnes of RSS3 rubber for nearby delivery while up to 1,800 tonnes of July/September RSS1 rubber was also bought, traders said.
"There was some shortcovering, but if you look at the rest of the market, it remains thin," a dealer said.
"It's a sleepy market. Just let sleeping dogs lie," another rubber trader said.
Traders predict further shortcovering in the market before the market lapses into a snooze during the Christmas holidays.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 122.50-123.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.00 cents.
July/September RSS1 was seen at 186.00 Singapore cents (US$1.33) a kg from the previous 186.50 cents.
February TSR20 was seen at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.24) a kg from 172.25 cents.
